```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = "##")
```

Demonstrating the approximation of Frisch–Waugh–Lovell (FWL) theorem with
nonlinear regression residuals using `NNS.reg()` and `np`.

# Basic FWL result with OLS

```{r ols-100}
set.seed(123)
x1 = rnorm(100)
x2 = rnorm(100)
y1 = 1 + x1 - x2 + rnorm(100)

r1 = residuals(lm(y1 ~ x2))
r2 = residuals(lm(x1 ~ x2))

# ols
coef(lm(y1 ~ x1 + x2))

# fwl ols
coef(lm(r1 ~ -1 + r2))
```

```{r packages, message = FALSE}
require(NNS)
require(data.table)
require(np)
options(np.messages = FALSE)
```

# NNS Residuals to Capture $\beta_1$

Step 1: NNS regression y1 on x2 and store residuals

```{r step1}
nns_r1 = NNS.reg(x2, y1, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals
```

Step 2: NNS regression x1 on x2 and store residuals

```{r step2}
nns_r2 = NNS.reg(x2, x1, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals
```

Step 3: OLS of NNS residuals is very close to $\beta_1$ of the FWL result

```{r step3}
lm(nns_r1 ~ nns_r2)
```

Step 4: Reverse x1 and x2 for the $\beta_2$ FWL result

```{r step4}
nns_r1 = NNS.reg(x1, y1, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals

nns_r2 = NNS.reg(x1, x2, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals

lm(nns_r1 ~ nns_r2)
```

## Step 4a: Let's check np

```{r np-100}
# Beta 1
np_1 = npreg(y1 ~ x2, residuals = TRUE)$resid

np_2 = npreg(x1 ~ x2, residuals = TRUE)$resid

coef(lm(np_1 ~ np_2))

# Beta 2
np_1 = npreg(y1 ~ x1, residuals = TRUE)$resid

np_2 = npreg(x2 ~ x1, residuals = TRUE)$resid

coef(lm(np_1 ~ np_2))
```

# Increase the number of observations

```{r n-1000}
set.seed(123)
x1 = rnorm(1000)
x2 = rnorm(1000)
y1 = 1 + x1 - x2 + rnorm(1000)

r1 = residuals(lm(y1 ~ x2))
r2 = residuals(lm(x1 ~ x2))
# ols
coef(lm(y1 ~ x1 + x2))

# nns Beta 1
nns_r1 = NNS.reg(x2, y1, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals

nns_r2 = NNS.reg(x2, x1, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals

lm(nns_r1 ~ nns_r2)

# nns Beta 2
nns_r1 = NNS.reg(x1, y1, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals

nns_r2 = NNS.reg(x1, x2, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals

lm(nns_r1 ~ nns_r2)

# np Beta 1
np_1 = npreg(y1 ~ x2, residuals = TRUE)$resid

np_2 = npreg(x1 ~ x2, residuals = TRUE)$resid

coef(lm(np_1 ~ np_2))

# np Beta 2
np_1 = npreg(y1 ~ x1, residuals = TRUE)$resid

np_2 = npreg(x2 ~ x1, residuals = TRUE)$resid

coef(lm(np_1 ~ np_2))
```

lm(nns_r1 ~ nns_r2)

nns_r1 = NNS.reg(x1, y1, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals

# Completely Different Functional Form

```{r nonlinear}
set.seed(123)
x1 = runif(1000)
x2 = runif(1000)
y1 = x1^2 * x2^2 + runif(1000)

r1 = residuals(lm(y1 ~ x2))
r2 = residuals(lm(x1 ~ x2))

# ols
coef(lm(y1 ~ x1 + x2))

# nns Beta 1
nns_r1 = NNS.reg(x2, y1, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals

nns_r2 = NNS.reg(x2, x1, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals

lm(nns_r1 ~ nns_r2)

# nns Beta 2
nns_r1 = NNS.reg(x1, y1, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals

nns_r2 = NNS.reg(x1, x2, plot = FALSE)$Fitted.xy$residuals

lm(nns_r1 ~ nns_r2)

# np Beta 1
np_1 = npreg(y1 ~ x2, residuals = TRUE)$resid

np_2 = npreg(x1 ~ x2, residuals = TRUE)$resid

coef(lm(np_1 ~ np_2))

# np Beta 2
np_1 = npreg(y1 ~ x1, residuals = TRUE)$resid

np_2 = npreg(x2 ~ x1, residuals = TRUE)$resid

coef(lm(np_1 ~ np_2))
```

> **Note (2026).** With $y = x_1^2 x_2^2 + u$ there is no single linear
> coefficient to recover: the slope of residual on residual is a
> best-linear-approximation summary of a conditional relationship, not a
> structural $\beta$ (see the residualization section of
> `examples/revised-companions.Rmd`).
